title: Fayette County, KY Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due
content:
Fayette County, KY Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kentucky
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Fayette County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Fayette County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Kentucky statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Fayette County, Kentucky property tax involves the county assessment office and the county sheriff. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who to contact in Fayette County

  • Fayette County Sheriff - Property Tax Division bills and collects the tax and handles delinquent tax.
  • Fayette County Property Valuation Administrator handles assessment and appeals.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Homestead exemption application is filed with the county PVA (state DOR) (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • 2026 bills: 10/01/2026-11/01/2026 2% discount; 01/01/2027-01/31/2027 5% penalty; 02/01/2027-04/15/2027 10% penalty + 10% add-on; mailed payments accepted for amount due on postmark date (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Bills not paid by April 15, 2027 become delinquent (21% penalty) and transfer to the Fayette County Clerk for collection (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)
  • Delinquent bills paid to County Clerk by cash, money order or cashier/certified check only; no personal/business checks or credit cards (from the county site listing; confirm with the office)

Assessment appeals

Owners can appeal to the county Property Valuation Administrator, then the county board of assessment appeals and the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals. Confirm the current deadline. See the Kentucky property tax guide.

Tax rate

We could not confirm a current county rate on an opened official page. Kentucky bills combine county, municipal and school district levies.

Selling in Fayette County?
We buy Fayette County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Fayette PVA appeal/conference dates and Board of Assessment Appeals filing window

How to sell a house in Fayette County

  1. Find out what the closing attorney needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Kentucky.

What a cash sale of a Fayette County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Fayette County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Kentucky disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Fayette County

  • Ask the tax collector what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Kentucky change, so confirm details with the official office or a Kentucky attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Fayette County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Fayette County property tax guide FAQ

Who handles assessment appeals in Fayette County?

Appeals go to the PVA, then the county board of assessment appeals.

What happens to unpaid Fayette County property tax when I sell?

The title company pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds at closing.

Union County, Kentucky property tax involves the county assessment office and the county sheriff. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who to contact in Union County

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Listed PVA website: www.unionpva.com
  • Bills mailed first week of October. Schedule: 2% discount Oct 1-Nov 1; face Nov 2-Dec 31; 5% penalty Jan 1-31; 10% penalty plus 10% sheriff add-on Feb 1-Apr 15; weekend due dates extend to following Monday; postmark on due date accepted
  • Delinquent bills transfer to County Clerk at close of business April 15; clerk payments carry 20% county attorney fee, 10% clerk fee and 1%/month interest; delinquency may be sold to a third party the following summer
  • Pay in person or mail to P.O. Box 30, Morganfield, KY 42437; cash (in office only), check, money order, credit card (3% fee); online search via vendor view.properlytaxes.com
  • Statewide (KY Dept of Revenue): taxpayers who conferred with the PVA must file the appeal at the county clerk's office by close of business the day after the last day of the tax roll inspection period; deadline is one workday after the inspection period ends

Assessment appeals

Owners can appeal to the county Property Valuation Administrator, then the county board of assessment appeals and the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals. Confirm the current deadline. See the Kentucky property tax guide.

Tax rate

We could not confirm a current county rate on an opened official page. Kentucky bills combine county, municipal and school district levies.

We buy Union County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Kentucky.

  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency.
